title: And the ones that did not come back

cues.text: You will recognise this picture instantly, because it is the hysteresis one. Same scale, same lines. Only the direction is different.
A firm that is already running.
The crisis arrives, and its takings fall.
Down past the level where the textbook would have closed it. And still it holds on, because holding on keeps the chance of recovery alive.
And then through the quit line. It closes.
Now the policy works. Conditions come back up to normal. All the way back to where they started.
The firm does not come back. Because coming back means paying the whole set-up cost over again.
State it plainly. What the policy stops from happening does not need explaining.
What needs explaining is why, for the firms it did not reach in time, nothing came back.
a firm absorbs losses, then closes
and the firm does not come back
because coming back costs the set-up again
